title: Movies to see this week: 'White Christmas,' 'Princess Bride' in concert - NewsBreak
text:
By Dustin Nelson ,
3 hours ago
Thanksgiving week makes for a lighter movie schedule, at least as far as older movies are concerned.
Theaters are clearing space for blockbusters like "Wicked: For Good" and "Zootopia," as well as the start of Oscar-bait season. (Hey, "Nuremberg.")
But there's still plenty of John Candy, Andre the Giant, and Ryan Phillippe to go around. Here are the movies you should catch at Twin Cities theaters this week.
'Planes, Trains and Automobiles' (1987) Wednesday, Nov. 26–Sunday, Nov. 30, at various theaters
It's Thanksgiving, so it's time for a viewing of "Planes, Trains and Automobiles." John Candy and Steve Martin star in the buddy comedy about a road trip home for the holiday. There will be plenty of chances to see it. It's playing at the Alamo Drafthouse, Parkway Theater, and St. Michael Cinema.
Minnesota Orchestra's 'The Princess Bride' (1987) in Concert Friday, Nov. 28–Sunday, Nov. 30, at Orchestra Hall
When I think of movies that typically get a full orchestra live score, I think of familiar soundtracks like "Jaws" or "Star Wars," or maybe even more recent movies with splashy names attached, like "There Will Be Blood."
The Minnesota Orchestra, however, thinks of fencing, fairy tales, Andre the Giant, and Wallace Shawn.
'The Way of the Gun' (2000) Friday, Nov. 28–Sunday, Nov. 30, at The Trylon Cinema
Tom Cruise's go-to director, Christopher McQuarrie, made his directorial debut with this very '00s shootout about two criminals — Benicio Del Toro and Ryan Phillippe — who kidnap a pregnant woman (Juliette Lewis) and hold her for ransom. However, they didn't understand the depths of the criminal ties involved in their scheme. Come for the winding plot, stay for the surprising Sarah Silverman appearance and a menacing James Caan.
"White Christmas" (1954)
Saturday, Nov. 29–Sunday, Dec. 7, at Heights Theater
So begins the Heights' annual run of "White Christmas," the classic holiday movie from director Michael Curtiz, starring Bing Crosby, Rosemary Clooney, and Danny Kaye. There will be pre-movie holiday music on the stage before each screening.
'Brazil' (1985) Director's Cut Monday, Dec. 1, at Alamo Drafthouse
Most of the movies featured here have live music or some kind of seasonal tie. This one, well, it's just "Brazil." The Alamo will show the director's cut of Terry Gilliam's surreal fever dream.
Related: Prince, Bob Dylan among Record Store Day releases. Here are the participating stores.
